subject: SLA variance request — filtering-toolchain regressions & fallback readiness
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@luma-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Theo Barnes <theo.barnes@luma-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: content-filter caused tool-call failure in production — request for SLA variance

Hi Olga / Laura,

We ran into a production incident this morning where our content moderation filter chain rejected several structured-output tool-calls, which cascaded into partial failures for our ingestion pipeline. The symptom: requests that should have returned structured JSON with external tool calls instead returned a filter-triggered 403 variant and the model fell back to a truncated text blob. This caused 14% of requests in the 07:30–08:00 PST window to fail validation downstream.

We've attached a CSV with the request ids and timestamps (luma_incident_logs_20270308.csv).

We understand filters are part of the platform safety posture, but because this affected our live models' tool-calling and structured outputs, we need to discuss a temporary SLA variance (latency/availability carve-out) while the root cause is investigated and mitigated. Specifically, we need: 
- Confirmation of whether this is a regression in Redwood's filtering logic or a change in model behavior
- A plan to enable a controlled fallback (safe-logged bypass or alternate model variant) so our critical ingestion doesn't drop messages in the interim
- Proposed timeline and communications cadence

From our side: this incident materially impacted downstream analytics and a scheduled billing job. We would like a short call today to align on the mitigation approach and to document an agreed SLA variance window.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Monroe
Head of MLOps, Luma Analytics
[attachment: luma_incident_logs_20270308.csv (csv, 88KB)]
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@luma-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: content-filter caused tool-call failure in production — request for SLA variance

Hi Alice — thanks for the detailed report and the CSV.

First, I'm sorry you hit this in production. We take any unplanned filtering-induced failures seriously. We will treat this as a joint incident and prioritize a short-term mitigation + triage plan. Next steps from Redwood: 

1) Rishi (SRE/runtime) will lead an immediate triage to determine whether the filter change was a rules/heuristic update or model-driven behaviour. He'll review the KV traces and filtering decision logs.
2) We can offer a controlled fallback policy while we investigate: for a specified window (you propose up to 72 hours), requests that hit the filter and were flagged only at the structured-output/tool-call layer can be routed to a "safe-failover" path. That path will: 
   - Return the best-effort structured output (with a stamped moderation label) instead of outright blocking;
   - Emit enhanced audit logs to both teams;
   - Throttle the fallback to a small percentage initially (canary) and increase if stable.
3) If the fallback is acceptable, we can document an SLA variance that excludes these filter-driven failures from uptime calculations for the agreed window.

Can you confirm the maximum tolerance window you need for the variance and whether a 5PM PST check-in today works for a short run-through? Rishi — after you review their logs, please outline quick mitigation options and the runbook link.

Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0117

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@luma-analytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: content-filter caused tool-call failure in production — request for SLA variance

Thanks, everyone — I dug into the attached sample IDs and pulled the runtime traces. Preliminary findings:

- The filter decision is being triggered at the post-generation moderation step when the model attempts to emit the tool-call JSON. There are two likely causes: an upstream prompt/context change that nudges token sequences closer to blocked patterns, or a tightened heuristic threshold that started evaluating more aggressively.
- I attached a trimmed kv trace with the moderation verdicts we recorded (runtime_kv_trace_0309.txt). The verdicts show the decision path and the ruleset id (ruleset_v12b).

Mitigation options (quick wins):
- Canary fallback policy (recommended): route up to 5% of affected requests to a "soft-allow" path that returns the structured output but includes an additional moderation flag in the headers/body. This keeps downstream validation but avoids drops.
- Alternate model variant: switch affected customers to model-variant m-v2-no-filter for the ingestion endpoint (quantized variant with same spec but with moderation checks disabled). Requires opt-in and has compliance implications.
- Prompt-scrubbing layer: implement a light pre-send transformation that masks sensitive tokens known to trigger the ruleset; low-lift but may reduce fidelity.

Operational constraints: we cannot enable an unlogged full bypass in production because of policy/audit requirements. Any fallback path must produce audit logs and be traceable.

Proposed timeline:
- Today (by 17:00 PST): enable canary soft-allow (5%) with enhanced logs and notify both teams.
- 24 hours: assess canary metrics; expand to 20% if error rates decrease and no safety incidents.
- 72 hours: full roll-forward to pre-incident routing or revert, depending on the root cause fix.

I'll open an internal incident ticket and link the runbook here: https://redwood-internal.company/runbooks/filter-fallback

Attaching the runtime trace: runtime_kv_trace_0309.txt

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Theo Barnes <theo.barnes@luma-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@luma-analytics.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-11T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: content-filter caused tool-call failure in production — request for SLA variance

Olga / Rishi — thanks for the quick triage and the concrete plan. We discussed internally and we're prepared to accept the proposed canary soft-allow approach for a limited window, with the following conditions: 

- Variance window: start 2027-03-09T17:00:00-07:00 (canary start) through 2027-03-12T17:00:00-07:00 (72 hours), during which filter-driven failures are excluded from SLA uptime calculations for our ingestion endpoint.
- We require hourly incident updates for the first 12 hours, then 3x daily after that.
- All fallback events must include the full audit payload and the moderation verdict id (ruleset id) in the logs.

Please send a short confirmation note and the signed variance statement (we can sign in DocuSign) — we'll consider this accepted once we have the variance doc and see the canary running.

Thanks,
Theo Barnes
Director, MLOps — Luma Analytics
